newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria foreign minister quits, party row deepens.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria foreign minister quits, party row deepens.

text.p: Bulgaria's Foreign Minister Georgi Pirinski, a prominent critic of Prime Minister Zhan Videnov, resigned on Wednesday saying the government did not have enough support to continue ruling.
His resignation came a day after Videnov won a narrow victory over his Socialist party critics in a confidence vote.
"The government does not have even the required minimum of confidence it needs to continue ruling," Pirinski told reporters.
At the end of a marathon 20-hour meeting on Tuesday, 87 members of the party leadership backed Videnov in a confidence vote, 69 voted against him and two abstained.
Three members of the party's executive bureau resigned at the meeting, including vice chairman Yanaki Stoilov.

The pro-Western reformist Pirinski is often cited as a potential challenger to Videnov for the prime minister's job and he is now well placed to challenge the premier at a full party congress scheduled for December 21 and 22.
The opposition says it will press for early parliamentary elections in the hope of unseating the Socialists, who are half way through their four-year term.
The Constitutional Court barred Pirinski from running for the presidency in elections last month because he was born in the United States.
The Socialists then picked Culture Minister Ivan Marazov, whose resounding defeat widened rifts within the party and prompted fresh calls for policy reforms and a new cabinet.

State radio quoted Videnov as saying he would name a new foreign minister by the end of next month and one of Pirinski's deputies would carry out his duties until then under the premier's supervision.
The party plenum backed Videnov's support for a currency board proposed by the International Monetary Fund to halt the collapse of the Bulgarian currency and stabilise the economy.

The lev, which started the year at 70 to the dollar, touched 260 on Wednesday. The Confederation of Independent Trade Unions plans a one-day general strike on December 4 to protest against falling living standards.

The IMF has twice postponed a badly-needed $115 million credit due to Bulgaria's failure to meet reform targets. Agreement with the Fund is vital if the Balkan state is to avoid defaulting on its $10 billion foreign debt.
